summary_md: **Steins ([@FooSteins](https://x.com/FooSteins/status/2116743392067748099))** summarizes *Memory Tax* by Xuan He and team at UIUC ([arXiv 2610.34073](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.34073), [project](https://hexuan21.github.io/MemoryTax/)): across 11 memory systems, 3 benchmarks and 3 backbones, 90 of 99 results fell below plain RAG over raw history, usually at higher token cost; net value is memory benefit minus memory tax, and much of the tax arises when summarizing drops details at write time.

referenced_urls.title: Memory Tax: Dissecting the Net Value of Agent Memory

relevance: Evidence that agent memory often underperforms RAG.

media.description: Accuracy versus token-cost Pareto bubble chart on LongMemEval-s with Qwen3.6-27B, placing RAG baselines against memory systems such as MemOS, HippoRAG2, A-Mem, LightMem, MAGMA, MemoryOS and OpenViking.
Histograms of the number of retrieval rounds needed to recover evidence per query on LongMemEval-s for RAG and five memory systems.
Bar chart of original performance, gains with gold memory, and remaining "memory tax" for RAG and memory systems on LongMemEval-s (Q27B) and PersonaMem-v2 (Q4B).
